paragraphs.en: The emergency drill began when a passerby reported a fictional accident outside the hospital. A contingent of volunteers assembled beside the main entrance, including a local patron who had funded new equipment. “Follow me,” the coordinator said, raising a fist so that those at the rear could see. A lad carrying a raincoat hurried over with his nephew. The point of the exercise was not to stage a heroic rescue, but to discover where ordinary procedures might fail before real danger arrived.
paragraphs.zh: 应急演练从一位路人报告医院外的模拟事故开始。一队志愿者在主入口旁集合，其中包括资助新设备的本地支持者。协调员举起拳头，让后面的人也看得见，并喊道：“跟我来。”一个小伙子带着侄子，拿着雨衣匆匆赶到。演练的重点不是表演英雄式救援，而是在真正危险来临前，找出日常流程可能失效的地方。

paragraphs.en: In the training room, a model showed how a rib protected the chest, an artery carried blood, and the spine supported movement. A nurse pointed to the skull, jaw, brow, and forehead, then asked trainees to describe what they could observe without pretending to make a medical diagnosis. Another model displayed a thigh muscle and part of the bowel. Accurate language mattered: a vague complaint about the belly could mean something different from pain in the upper part of the trunk. Yet careful listening remained more useful than impressive terminology alone.
paragraphs.zh: 培训室里的模型显示肋骨怎样保护胸部、动脉怎样输送血液，以及脊柱怎样支撑活动。护士指着头骨、下颌、眉部和额头，请受训者描述自己能观察到的情况，而不要假装进行医学诊断。另一个模型展示了大腿肌肉与部分肠道。准确语言很重要：笼统地说肚子不舒服，可能与躯干上部疼痛不是一回事。但再漂亮的术语，也不能取代认真倾听。

paragraphs.en: The actors played residents with different needs. One patient said she felt cold and ill; another described a symptom that had interrupted sleep for several nights. A father worried about a child born with a health condition, while an orphan had no adult to contact. Staff practiced keeping each person safe and protecting privacy. A recorded temperature was information, not a complete explanation, and a damaged cell in a diagram could not tell the whole story of a disease. The exercise discouraged easy promises of a cure.
paragraphs.zh: 演员扮演有不同需求的居民。一位病人说自己发冷、身体不适；另一位描述连续几晚影响睡眠的症状。一位父亲担心患先天健康问题的孩子，一个孤儿则没有可以联系的成年人。工作人员练习保障每个人的安全与隐私。体温记录提供信息，却不是完整解释；图上受损的细胞也无法讲清一种疾病的全部情况。演练强调，不应轻易许诺治愈。

paragraphs.en: A gay volunteer played a worried partner and noticed how often forms assumed a conventional household. A retired teacher, addressed as “madam,” said she preferred her name. The archive behind the training room still contained old labels such as “maiden” and “mistress,” reminders that official language could carry social judgments. A comrade from a mutual-aid group asked why volunteers were described as a gang in one draft notice. “This is work by all of us,” he said. “Let the words reflect that.”
paragraphs.zh: 一位同性恋志愿者扮演忧心的伴侣，发现表格常常默认传统家庭结构。一位被称为“女士”的退休教师说，她更喜欢别人叫名字。培训室后面的档案还保留着“未婚女子”“情妇”之类的旧标签，提醒人们官方语言也可能包含社会评判。互助组织的一位同伴追问，为何通知草稿把志愿者称为“帮伙”。他说：“这是我们所有人的工作，措辞也应该体现这一点。”

paragraphs.en: The final discussion concerned the difference between providing medicine and providing reassurance. No volunteer could decide which drug would treat cancer, and nobody should announce a death without proper authority. One scenario involved a dead phone battery, leaving a relative unable to reach him. Another left a family uncertain how to contact them after a transfer. “The responsibility is yours as well as ours,” the coordinator concluded. Care depended on reliable communication, not merely on a dramatic performance under pressure. At the review, participants chose three failures to address first and assigned clear responsibilities, because identifying weaknesses would mean little if the same obstacles remained when a real incident occurred.
paragraphs.zh: 最后的讨论聚焦于提供药物与给予安心感之间的差别。志愿者不能自行决定用什么药治疗癌症，也不应越权宣布死亡。一个情境设定为手机电池耗尽，亲属无法联系到当事人；另一个则让家人在转院后不知道怎样取得联系。协调员总结说：“责任既属于我们，也属于你们。”照护依赖可靠的沟通，而不只是压力下的精彩表现。复盘时，参与者选出三项问题优先解决，并明确责任，因为如果真实事故发生时障碍依旧，找出弱点也没有多少意义。
